subject: POC prompt/log sample spec + data security agreement
body:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@databridge.com>, Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@databridge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: POC prompt/log sample spec + data security agreement

Hi Oliver / Emma —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can kick off the POC cleanly:

1) What we need from you (deliverables)
   - Prompt/log sample bundle: 1,500 anonymized prompt+response pairs (CSV preferred). See attached prompt_sample_schema.csv for exact columns.
   - For logs that include multi-turn sessions, please include session_id and timestamp.
   - A short list (10–20) of high-priority test prompts that represent your hardest user journeys.

2) POC success criteria (draft) — we'll finalize together:
   - Intent accuracy >= 85% on the held-out prompt set (micro-averaged intent labels).
   - Hallucination incidence <= 5% (as measured on a 300-sample manual review).
   - Generation latency P50 < 250ms, P95 < 600ms for 256-token responses in our dedicated environment.
   - Cost target: average per-request token cost below your current baseline by 20% (measured across the evaluation window).

3) Evaluation plan / how we'll score:
   - You provide the prompt/log samples and label file (if available). Redwood will create a 70/30 split for train/holdout unless you request otherwise.
   - We will run a deterministic evaluation pass and produce: confusion matrix, precision/recall/F1 for intents, hallucination flagging report, and latency/cost dashboards.
   - For hallucination measurement we will run an automated filter + 300 human checks (we'll share the review rubric).

4) Data handling & security:
   - Please redact direct PII where possible. If redaction is not feasible, mark fields as SENSITIVE and we will treat them as encrypted payloads and keep them only on customer-only S3 for the POC.
   - We'll share a DPA draft (attached) for your legal. If you prefer we can route the DPA via DocuSign — link included below.

5) Timeline (proposal):
   - Dec 18: you deliver sample bundle and labels (or confirm shared Drive link).
   - Dec 20–23: Redwood ingestion + initial eval run.
   - Jan 4: delivery of full evaluation report + results review call.

6) Owners / points of contact:
   - DataBridge: Oliver Grant (technical lead), Emma Lewis (product).
   - Redwood: Tessa Morgan (sales owner) tessa.morgan@redwood.com, Vivek Kulkarni (solutions/serving) vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, Sean Gallagher (customer success) sean.gallagher@redwood.com.

7) Logistics / transfer options:
   - Preferred: secure upload to the Drive folder we shared (link below) with link-level restriction.
   - Alternate: S3 pre-signed upload to a customer-specific bucket; we can provide upload credentials.

Attachments: prompt_sample_schema.csv (CSV schema example), poc-success-criteria.md (draft), redwood-dpa-draft.pdf

A few questions for you to confirm on the reply:
   - Can the sample bundle exclude raw emails/logs with unredacted PII?
   - Do you prefer the Drive upload or S3?
   - Any additional acceptance criteria we should include for the POC?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min sync if that's easier.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Rep, Redwood Inference
T +1 (415) 555-0198

-----Original Message-----
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@databridge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@databridge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC prompt/log sample spec + data security agreement

Tessa —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. We can get you the 1,500 rows but a couple clarifications:

- A lot of our logs currently include user identifiers and freeform text with PII. We will try to run a redaction pass but may not be able to remove everything by Dec 18. Is it ok if we tag sensitive fields and upload an encrypted bundle?
- For the high-priority prompts, we'll send 12 examples from our support flows.
- Drive upload is fine. Can you confirm the folder permissions: link-only vs. account-restricted?

We will also loop in procurement (procurement@databridge.com) to get a quick review on the DPA.

Oliver
Director of Data Products | DataBridge Inc
oliver.grant@databridge.com | +1 (917) 555-2255

On Mon, Dec 14, 2027 at 12:45 PM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:

> Hi all — quick note on the evaluation side:
>
> - If DataBridge must upload fields that are labeled SENSITIVE, we will ingest them into a customer-isolated S3 folder and enable at-rest encryption + limited retention (default 30 days post-POC) unless you request otherwise.
> - For model config, we've found quantization + prefix caching is a good default for support-style prompts; I'll propose a candidate config once we see token length distribution.
> - Regarding the success criteria, adding a qualitative customer satisfaction target (e.g., triage reduction on support tickets by 10%) could be helpful if you have baseline metrics.
>
> Vivek
> Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood
> vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
>
On Tue, Dec 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:

> Perfect — thanks Oliver. A few quick confirmations:
>
> - Drive folder will be account-restricted (we'll invite the three uploader emails you give us). I'll send the invite once you confirm the uploader list.
> - Encryption and tagged-sensitive-field handling is fine — Vivek will set the ingestion config.
> - Procurement: thanks for looping them in. We'll expect comments on the DPA by Dec 20.
>
> Next step: Oliver/Emma, can you confirm which date you prefer for delivering the sample bundle (Dec 18 or Dec 21)? If you pick Dec 21 we'll shift the evaluation window by 3 business days and still aim for the early Jan report.
>
> I'll slot a 30-min kickoff on Jan 5 at 10am PT for the post-eval review unless you prefer a different time.
>
> --
> Tessa
